name: Dholl Puri

ingredients.name: curry powder without onion or garlic

steps: Soak the split peas for 2 hours, then drain and rinse them.
Simmer the peas in the measured cooking water for about 25 minutes until just tender. Drain very thoroughly, cool, then grind to a fine dry crumb with cumin, turmeric and 4 g salt.
Knead the flour, 4 g salt, 15 ml oil and warm dough water until soft and smooth. Cover and rest for 20 minutes while making the accompaniments.

For the bean curry, heat 25 ml oil and stir in grated ginger and curry powder for 30 seconds. Add butter beans, passata, bean-curry water and 4 g salt; simmer 12–15 minutes until thick enough to spoon.
For the tomato chutney, finely dice fresh tomatoes and chop coriander and chilli. Mix with lime juice and remaining 2 g salt; stand for 10 minutes to meld the flavours.
Divide dough into eight balls. Fill each with a spoonful of ground split peas, pinch closed and roll gently into a very thin round without tearing.
Cook each filled round on a hot griddle for about 1 minute per side, brushing with the remaining 20 ml oil. Fold each warm dholl puri around bean curry and fresh tomato chutney; serve two per person.
tips: Grind the cooked split peas finely and keep them dry; damp, coarse filling tears the thin flatbread. Keep the bean curry thick so it does not soak through.
passiveTime: Soak split peas for 2 hours before cooking.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
